CHANGED at stage 4 (was “库法”（quffa）). 库法 is an attested Chinese name of the city of Kufa: zh.wikipedia titles the city 库费 and its lead reads «库费（阿拉伯语：الكوفة）……又译库法», with 库法 redirecting there. Ruling ZH-W2 forbids coining a Chinese transliteration for a foreign generic noun (a tool) that has no attestation in a published Chinese source, and the table form 古法 is a Chinese word. So the word stays Latin in Chinese quotation marks, once, next to the source's own definition (since judge loop 1 the definition precedes the word: 用椰枣树枝叶做成的篮子“quffa”). Precedent on the site: the Tarafa article keeps qasaba, sahifa and hisy in Latin with the source's explanation. This departs from the brief's «quffa كذلك»; the fallback, if the judge wants a Chinese handle, is “库法”（quffa） as in stage 3. [house-derived]

additions.judge: Judge 2026-11-27: Latin-only “quffa” upheld; “库法”（quffa） is rejected for good (库法 is Kufa; ZH-W2), which overrules the brief on this one word. After blind-reader note 5 the source's definition now stands before the word: 他还把用椰枣树枝叶做成的篮子“quffa”放在这两块里，用来存放大米和咖啡.

A phrase search for 阿巴亚 showed only the Brazilian place name 阿巴亚拉 in the results returned; no garment hit was seen. Mainland press mostly writes 黑袍 or «Abaya长袍»; Xinhua 2024 has 黑袍. 长袍 attached as in 比什特长袍 (ZH-W2); no colour word. 哈萨 is repeated before the second noun because in the Arabic الأحسائية governs both nouns, and the bound string 哈萨比什特长袍 would otherwise leave the abayas unmarked. [verified]
additions.judge: Judge 2026-11-27: 哈萨 repeated before the second noun is kept (the Arabic adjective governs both nouns; the bound string 哈萨比什特长袍 cannot be broken).
